# Fanon — Peau noire, masques blancs

## Bibliographic identity and consulted object

Frantz Fanon's French work appeared with Éditions du Seuil in1952. The consulted object is Émilie Tremblay's electronic edition for Les Classiques des sciences sociales, dated **6 December2011** on PDF p.5. Its title and edition pages identify Seuil1952,239pages and include Francis Jeanson's1952 preface and1965 postface. This is a260-page electronic resetting, **not a facsimile of the1952 first edition**. The electronic edition's bibliographic formulation does not establish which later print state supplied every page. Jeanson's later paratext is not assigned to1952.

The canonical local PDF identified by `local_copy` above preserves the actual previously consulted bytes. One-based **PDF page numbers** below identify this object. Bracketed **print markers reproduced in the electronic text** provide a second locator system; these have not been independently collated against a physical printing. They must never be substituted for the PDF page number.

The existing political-theory-institutions domain houses this colonial political and social inquiry; its psychiatric, phenomenological and psychological operations remain explicit in the reading. Filing does not reduce the work to an institutional treatise.

## Reading scope and source operation

Full material reading completed for the introduction, chaptersI,V,VII and conclusion; frontmatter PDF1–9 was read for edition identity. Unchanged source hashes permit reuse of that reading. ChaptersII–IV andVI and the Jeanson paratext are **not** claimed read in full. No English translation has been selected or collated, and the English paraphrases here are not quotations or an admitted published translation.

Language admits the Antillean speaker into a socially valued world while exposing him to its racialised standard. The lived bodily inquiry distinguishes the body-schema, historically supplied racial image and epidermal racial schema. Recognition then encounters socially unequal conditions which cannot be removed through private self-description alone. The conclusion returns the inquiry to material situations and future-directed human freedom. These different chapter movements support the [Fanon whole](../../../../../mytheme/worlds/francophone-anticolonial/fanon-language-gaze-mask-recognition/WHOLE.md#fanon-whole); they are not presented as one continuous fictional scene.

## Passage card — `fanon-1952-peau-noire-masques-blancs-q002` — I — Le Noir et le langage
^fanon-1952-peau-noire-masques-blancs-q002

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** Speaking entails a relation to the other and to a civilisation with socially assigned value. ## Passage card — `fanon-1952-peau-noire-masques-blancs-q004` — V — The train and racial hail within that movement
^fanon-1952-peau-noire-masques-blancs-q004

> **Paraphrase (not a quotation):** Repeated public designation and the child’s fear alter the space of encounter. Responsibility for body, race and ancestors is imposed upon the person, and the practical body-schema gives way to an epidermal racial schema. This local scene inherits the whole chapter’s history and unresolved aftermath.

## Admission completed and remaining boundaries

The missing canonical French source house and referenced local-copy debts are fulfilled. The selected five material scopes are admitted, with the train scene additionally indexed inside chapterV. The complete work and later paratext have not been declared fully read. English translation selection, exact quotation collation and any extension into unexamined chapters remain separate tasks.

The whole's four inherited comparisons—adaptive interface, category before encounter, Objective Co-Internality and idol/image—remain human-amplified:no. Source recovery does not ratify them. Neumann provides a distinct shared archetypal field; it neither supplies the colonial history nor places a people on a developmental stage. Fanon's language, schemata and recognition remain his source field, while QL/technical comparisons retain their project-authored standing.
